newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka sees surpassing '97 privatisation target.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka sees surpassing '97 privatisation target.

text.p: Sri Lanka is confident of netting more than its budgeted revenue targets from privatisations in 1997, Mano Tittawella, director general of the Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC), said on Tuesday.

"I am confident we will raise the five billion rupees needed to meet budgeted revenue targets in 1997, from plantation sector reforms and the sale of a few government minority holdings in companies," Tittawella told Reuters.
Privatisation of ownership of 23 regional estate firms, which began in late 1995, is expected to be completed this year, Tittawella said.
"The process, which includes selling 51 percent to a strategic investor and the balance to the public after giving 10 percent to employees, should net over four billion rupees."
Selling minority stakes in Lanka Ceramic and a few other firms should take the total to five billion, he said.
PERC expects the largest chunks of revenue to come from selling 40 percent and management of the ailing national carrier Airlanka and 35 percent and management of Sri Lanka Telecom.
Post-bid negotiations were being conducted on both AirLanka and Sri Lanka Telecom deals, with a final decision expected well within fiscal 1997, said Tittawella.
He said PERC was negotiating with six final bidders on Airlanka, including two Asian carriers, and Japan's NTT and France Telecom for Sri Lanka Telecom.
He declined to give financial details of the deal.
"All I will say is that we are confident of getting well in excess of the budgeted revenue target for 1997," Tittawella said.
